title: A parathyroid adenoma masquerading as an oesophageal cyst.
abstract: A male in his 60s presented with ventricular fibrillation arrest, severe hypercalcaemia and elevated parathyroid hormone levels. A diagnosis of primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT) was suspected. Initial imaging, including single-photon emission CT, failed to localise the suspected parathyroid adenoma (PTA). Further imaging review revealed a mediastinal cystic mass adjacent to the oesophagus. Thoracic surgery consultation was undertaken and it was felt the cyst was an unrelated duplication cyst. The patient continued to have uncontrolled calcium levels and therefore an exploratory parathyroidectomy was performed. Postoperative pathology confirmed the oesophageal cyst was a PTA. These cysts are associated with more severe clinical manifestations and higher calcium, likely due to delayed diagnosis and localisation. This case underscores the importance of using multiple imaging modalities for preoperative localisation, especially in atypical cases of PHPT. Mediastinal PTA, despite its extreme rarity, should be considered with incidental PHPT and a seemingly extraneous mediastinal mass.

title: Oral functional impairments associated with large sublingual angiolipoma.
abstract: A male patient in his late 50s presented with a long-standing, painless sublingual mass causing progressive impairment of speech, mastication, swallowing and intermittent respiratory discomfort due to restricted tongue mobility. An MRI demonstrated a well-circumscribed lipomatous lesion without evidence of significant vascular involvement, suggesting a conventional lipoma and facilitating surgical planning; however, definitive diagnosis remained uncertain preoperatively. The lesion was successfully excised through a transoral approach under intravenous sedation and local anaesthesia, with complete functional recovery and no recurrence during 6 months of follow-up. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of angiolipoma, highlighting the limitations of imaging in distinguishing lipomatous tumour subtypes and the importance of histopathological confirmation. This case emphasises that large benign lesions of the floor of the mouth may cause substantial functional impairment despite their indolent course, making timely recognition and surgical management essential.

title: Radial artery penetrating injury with a retained agave spine: diagnostic and surgical considerations.
abstract: This case report describes an interesting case of penetrating radial artery injury caused by a retained agave spine following minor gardening penetrating injury in a patient presented with progressive wrist pain and swelling. Doppler ultrasound demonstrated a radiolucent linear foreign body penetrating the radial artery without active bleeding. The foreign body was successfully removed via open surgical exploration under tourniquet control, with intraoperative ultrasound confirming complete retrieval and identifying a minor mural thrombus. The patient made an uncomplicated recovery with preserved arterial patency on follow-up. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of organic, radiolucent-retained foreign bodies emphasising the selection of appropriate imaging. It also discussed operative strategies and postoperative management with follow-up in seemingly minor penetrating extremity injuries.

title: Jejunal metastatic melanoma presenting with occult gastrointestinal haemorrhage and refractory anaemia.
abstract: Malignant melanoma is the most common tumour to metastasise to the gastrointestinal (GI) tract; however, symptomatic involvement is uncommon during life. We report a case of small bowel metastatic melanoma presenting as a large aneurysmal jejunal mass in an elderly man with chronic iron-deficiency anaemia and weight loss many years after excision of early-stage cutaneous melanomas. Despite cross-sectional imaging and endoscopic investigations, diagnosis remained uncertain until exploratory laparotomy was performed. En bloc resection of the jejunal segment with associated mesentery achieved complete excision and histopathology confirmed metastatic melanoma. Although molecular analysis identified a BRAF mutation, severe cardiac comorbidity precluded systemic therapy. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of GI melanoma metastasis, the uncharacteristic radiological appearance of aneurysmal dilatation and the continued role of surgical resection for symptom control and definitive diagnosis in selected patients.

title: Non-surgical management of post-traumatic internal and external inflammatory root resorption in an immature maxillary central incisor: 4-year follow-up.
abstract: Divergent pulpal responses following dental trauma may manifest as inflammatory resorption in one tooth and pulp canal obliteration (PCO) in other affected teeth. When such changes occur in an immature tooth with an open apex, diagnosis and treatment planning become particularly challenging. This case report describes a traumatised maxillary right central incisor in a young male patient with non-perforating internal root resorption (RR), external inflammatory RR and pulp necrosis, while the maxillary right lateral and left central incisors exhibited PCO. Cone-beam CT allowed precise definition of lesion extent and supported a conservative treatment strategy comprising chemomechanical disinfection with calcium hydroxide, placement of a mineral trioxide aggregate apical barrier and thermoplastic obturation. At the 48-month follow-up, the tooth was asymptomatic and functional, with imaging evidence of periapical healing and arrest of resorption. The biologically based conservative approach resulted in sustained function, satisfactory aesthetics and overall patient satisfaction.

title: Septal Nonischemic Late Gadolinium Enhancement After Myocardial Infarction Is Associated With Adverse Remodeling and Improves Risk Stratification for Heart Failure Outcomes.
abstract: Background The prevalence, anatomic distribution, enhancement patterns, and prognostic value of nonischemic late gadolinium enhancement (NI-LGE) in patients with prior myocardial infarction were not systematically investigated. Methods A total of 948 patients (mean±SD age, 56.2±10.9 years; 88.4% men) diagnosed with prior myocardial infarction by cardiac magnetic resonance imaging were analyzed, excluding those with coexisting nonischemic cardiomyopathies or myocarditis. NI-LGE was defined as midwall or subepicardial enhancement. Competing risk analysis was performed to mitigate the influence of competing events. Results Among these, NI-LGE was observed in 78 patients (8.2%), with septal involvement present in all cases. Lower left ventricular ejection fraction (odds ratio [OR]=0.97, P =0.01) and larger end-diastolic volume index (OR=1.01, P <0.001) were independently associated with NI-LGE. During a median follow-up of 69.6 months (interquartile range, 49.7-80.9 months), 99 (10.4%) and 63 (6.6%) experienced heart failure (HF)- and sudden cardiac death-related events, respectively. NI-LGE was associated with a markedly increased risk of HF-related events (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR]=5.98, P <0.001) after adjusting for the confounders, but not sudden cardiac death ( P =0.65). NI-LGE improved the model discrimination and fit performance (C-index: 0.84-0.87; likelihood ratio: 1168.0-1106.1, both P <0.001) for the HF-related events beyond left ventricular ejection fraction and late gadolinium enhancement extent. Moreover, NI-LGE involving both the septum and free wall conferred a higher risk of HF-related events than isolated septal involvement (sHR=2.42, P =0.02). Conclusions NI-LGE occurs in 8.2% of patients with prior myocardial infarction, predominantly involving the interventricular septum. As a potential marker of adverse remodeling, NI-LGE might provide incremental prognostic value for HF-related outcomes beyond traditional markers.

title: Are Endourologists More Likely to Definitively Treat Symptomatic Stones at Initial Presentation?
abstract: Introduction Ureteral stones are a common cause of emergency presentations. Definitive stone removal at the index encounter can reduce delays and repeat interventions. It is unknown whether fellowship-trained endourologists are more likely to perform definitive management than general/other subspecialist urologists. This multicenter retrospective cohort study evaluated the influence of endourology subspecialty training on the choice between upfront definitive stone treatment and initial ureteral decompression at first presentation. Patients managed with medical expulsive therapy alone were not included. Methods Adults (≥18 years) presenting at 2022 to seven North American academic centers with symptomatic, noninfected, computed tomography-confirmed ureteral stones were included. Patients with infection, sepsis, positive nitrites, or intraoperative pyelonephritis were excluded from the study. Variables included demographics, stone size and location, subspecialty of the on-call urologist, and management type (definitive [ureteroscopy or shockwave lithotripsy] vs deferred [(initial stent]). Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify the predictors of definitive treatment. Results Among the 395 patients, 190 (48.0%) underwent definitive management and 205 (52.0%) underwent deferred treatment. Distal stones were treated definitively more often than proximal stones were (51.1% vs 36.6%). An endourologist was on call for 150 encounters (38.0%); 64.7% of these patients received definitive treatment, compared with 38.0% under general/other subspecialist urologists. On multivariate analysis, endourologist on-call remained independently associated with definitive management (odds ratio [OR] 3.46, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.19-5.47, p < 0.0001), as did distal stone location (OR: 2.46, 95% CI: 1.21-5.00, p = 0.013). Severe complications are rare, and none of the patients developed sepsis. Conclusions Endourologists were more than three times more likely to perform definitive interventions for symptomatic, noninfected ureteral stones at initial presentation. Subspecialty expertise and timely operative access enable safe, efficient, single-stage management.

title: Synchronous Odontogenic Fibromyxoma and Compact Osteoma in a Pediatric Patient: A Rare Case Report Mimicking Ameloblastic Fibro-Odontoma.
abstract: Odontogenic myxoma is a rare, benign mesenchymal odontogenic neoplasm. Microscopically, odontogenic myxoma consists of spindle-shaped or stellate cells within an myxoid stroma. In rare tumors, the stroma contains heavy collagen deposition, and they are then termed odontogenic fibromyxomas. We report an unusual synchronous presentation of an odontogenic fibromyxoma and an osteoma in a 12-year-old boy, which clinically mimicked an ameloblastic fibro-odontoma. The patient presented with a left mandibular mass. Imaging revealed an extensive 51-mm osteolytic lesion accompanied by a hyperdense calcified mass. Radiographic findings were suggestive of an ameloblastic fibro-odontoma. A biopsy of the tumor was performed, and the calcified mass was excised. Histopathological analysis confirmed the diagnosis of an odontogenic fibromyxoma with an associated compact osteoma. The patient underwent a partial mandibular resection and remains disease-free at the 12-month follow-up. A synchronous occurrence of an odontogenic myxoma and an osteoma is rare and can mimic other lesions, making diagnosis challenging.

title: Mid- to long-term follow-up of trabecular titanium acetabular cups in hip revision surgery for acetabular bone defects.
abstract: Background Acetabular defects can be restored using different surgical techniques. Excellent results have been observed with trabecular titanium (TT) which mimic the structure of trabecular bone. The aim of our study is to evaluate the mid-to-long-term outcome in revision surgery due to severe acetabular defect using TT cups. Materials and methods We performed a retrospective analysis of patients undergoing revision with Paprosky IIa or higher using modular TT cup. We evaluated clinical outcomes using FJS, WOMAC, OHS, and WORQ. Radiolucency and integration were used to assess radiographic results. We collected information on complications and revisions. Results Data from 217 consecutive patients was collected. Mean age was 71,01 ± 11,40 years. In regard to diagnosis, patients were affected by: aseptic loosening (55,3%); debris-induced osteolysis (18%); infection (11,5%); PPF (7.8%); and dislocation (7.4%). At the final floow-up, we documented the following: OHS 35.06 ± 4,31; WORQ 26.69 ± 4.18; WOMAC 27.59 ± 7.57; FJS of 55.3 ± 10.39 ( p -value < 0.005). Complication rate was 9.2%. The most frequent complication was dislocation, followed by deep infection and aseptic loosening. The Kaplan-Meier survivorship curve showed a 96.3% rate of acetabular implant survival at 12 years. Discussion and conclusions This is the study with the largest population using TT for acetabular defects. We report good outcomes and an acceptable rate of complications, also due to implant modularity allowing stable fixation with secondary osseointegration.

title: Salvage reverse shoulder arthroplasty after failed plate fixation of proximal humeral fractures: Clinical outcomes, complications, and prognostic factors.
abstract: Background Failed plate fixation (open reduction and internal fixation) for proximal humeral fractures causes bone loss, tuberosity malunion, and soft-tissue imbalance. Reverse shoulder arthroplasty (RSA) is a salvage option with variable outcomes. This study evaluated RSA outcomes for fracture sequelae and previous plate fixation and identified prognostic factors. Methods This retrospective monocentric study included patients undergoing RSA between 2011 and 2023 for fracture sequelae following plate fixation, with a minimum two-year follow-up. Outcomes included clinical scores, range of motion, patient satisfaction, and radiographic findings. Prognostic factors were analyzed using univariate analysis. Results Twenty-nine patients were included (mean follow-up 4.6 years; mean age 59 years). Clinical scores and range of motion improved compared with the preoperative evaluation (all p < 0.05), except for external rotation. Final mean adjusted Constant score was 64%, Subjective Shoulder Value 56, and American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons (ASES) 65. Overall, 34% had complications, 10% required reoperation, and 7% underwent revision.The most common complication was persistent painful shoulder stiffness (21%). Humeral bone resorption in the previous plate area was observed in 50%. Greater tuberosity deficiency and anterior deltoid dysfunction were associated with worse outcomes. Conclusion RSA improves outcomes after failed plate fixation; however, recovery remains moderate, and complication rates are high. Tuberosity deficiency and anterior deltoid dysfunction are prognostic factors, and humeral bone resorption may affect long-term survival. Level of evidence Level IV; Case Series; Treatment Study.

title: The NorthMom study: population-based follow-up of women in a birth cohort to assess pregnancy exposures and effects on breast cancer risk factors.
abstract: Background The NorthMom Study (NorthMom) is an observational, population-based cohort designed to determine how the environment during pregnancy affects later health risks among women. The specific focus of NorthMom is breast cancer risk, evaluated through intermediate markers such as breast density, and additional outcomes may be studied in the future. Methods NorthMom is nested in the larger NorthPop Birth Cohort Study (NorthPop), which was initiated in Västerbotten County, Sweden in 2016 and closed recruitment in 2025. All women previously enrolled in NorthPop are invited to join NorthMom after turning 40 years of age. Women who have moved from the county, have withdrawn or declined follow-up from NorthPop, or are pregnant at the time of invitation are considered ineligible. Those who agree to participate visit the Clinical Research Center at the University Hospital of Umeå in Västerbotten, Sweden. A study nurse collects a blood sample and additional health data, including body composition by Dual-Energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). title: Dynamic [ 18 F]PI-2620 recording facilitates prediction of β-amyloid positivity and simultaneous staging of tau and neurodegeneration.
abstract: Background Patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD) and clinically overlapping neurodegenerative diseases are classified molecularly using the A/T/N classification system. Apart from fluid biomarkers and structural MRI, A/T/N assessment incorporates β-amyloid-PET (A), tau-PET (T), and [ 18 F]FDG-PET (N). We evaluated if dynamic features of tau-PET with [ 18 F]PI-2620 allow prediction of β-amyloid positivity and simultaneous staging of tau and neurodegeneration in individual patients using a single imaging session. Methods We studied 129 patients with tauopathies, comprising 47 patients with β-amyloid-positive 3/4-repeat tauopathy and 82 patients with β-amyloid-negative primary 4-repeat tauopathies, alongside 17 healthy controls. Participants underwent 60-minute dynamic [ 18 F]PI-2620 tau-PET. Kinetic modelling simultaneously provided tracer efflux rate (K2a) as a predictor for β-amyloid status, distribution volume ratio (DVR) for regional tau burden, and relative perfusion (R1) as a marker of neurodegeneration. These parameters were validated against β-amyloid-PET, [ 18 F]FDG-PET, volumetric MRI, and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers using receiver operating characteristic and correlation analyses and visual assessments. [ 18 F]PI-2620 K2a -based prediction of β-amyloid positivtiy was additionally tested in an independent, clinically heterogeneous validation cohort of 97 individuals. Results [ 18 F]PI-2620 K2a differentiated tau isoform compositions despite clinically overlapping presentations and tau-PET patterns, demonstrating reduced cortical tracer clearance in 3/4-repeat compared with 4-repeat tauopathies. [ 18 F]PI-2620 K2a remained sensitive in individuals with visually negative or low [ 18 F]PI-2620 DVR signals and outperformed both tau burden and perfusion for predicting β-amyloid status, achieving an area under the curve of 0.99, a positive predictive value of 91.5%, and a negative predictive value of 95.1%. Performance remained robust in the independent validation cohort, with an area under the curve of 0.98, a positive predictive value of 87.9%, and a negative predictive value of 95.3%. [ 18 F]PI-2620 DVR quantified regional tau patterns, with cortical predominance in 3/4-repeat tauopathy and subcortical involvement in 4-repeat tauopathies. [ 18 F]PI-2620 R1 exhibited strong quantitative and visual associations with established markers of neurodegeneration. Integration of K2a, DVR, and R1 in disease-specific composite regions enabled individualized three-dimensional A/T/N staging. Conclusions Dynamic [ 18 F]PI-2620 PET imaging facilitates assessment of the β-amyloid status and regional staging of tau and neurodegeneration during a single acquisition. This one-stop-shop approach may reduce radiation exposure, streamline diagnostic workflows, and facilitate personalized disease profiling.

title: Ultrasound Characteristics of the Infrapatellar Fat Pad Under Physiological and Pathological Conditions.
abstract: The infrapatellar fat pad (IFP) is an intracapsular, extra-synovial adipose tissue located beneath the patellar tendon. It serves as a protective cushion for the knee, mitigating the mechanical impact of various movements. Furthermore, the IFP possesses a robust vascular network and strong secretory capacity, enabling it to contribute to the resolution of various inflammatory processes associated with knee pathology. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is widely used to assess the IFP, but it is limited by high cost, long examination times, and an inability to provide real-time dynamic evaluation. Ultrasound offers a cost-effective, portable, and clinically accessible alternative for IFP imaging. Beyond visualizing the dynamic morphology of the IFP, advances in Doppler ultrasound and elastography now enable the assessment of blood supply and mechanical properties. This review summarizes the ultrasound features of the IFP under physiological and pathological conditions, explores its potential applications in the diagnosis and evaluation of IFP-related disorders, and highlights future directions, with particular emphasis on the role of dynamic ultrasound in evaluating anterior knee disorders in sports medicine.

title: Gap Between Estimated Need and Observed Uptake of Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors Among Patients With Lung Cancer in Indonesia.
abstract: Purpose In many low- and middle-income countries, access to molecularly targeted therapies for lung cancer remains limited. This study assessed the gap between estimated epidermal growth factor receptor-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (EGFR-TKI) treatment need and observed uptake in Indonesia and evaluated the gap before and after implementation of the National Reimbursement System (NRS). We hypothesized that many potentially eligible patients in Indonesia would not receive EGFR-TKI therapy, as they ideally should. Methods We retrospectively analyzed all patient cases of lung cancer registered between 2008 and 2020 at Indonesia's national referral hospital. Patients with a registered diagnosis verified by histopathology or supporting clinical evidence were included. Because patient-level molecular and clinical eligibility data were incomplete, EGFR-TKI eligibility was estimated using a stepwise epidemiologic model. A model-based sensitivity analysis was performed to assess robustness. Observed uptake was compared before and after NRS implementation. title: Giant Well-Differentiated Liposarcoma of the Spermatic Cord Associated With Inguinal Hernia: Clinical Insights From a Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND Spermatic cord liposarcoma is a rare adipocytic malignancy, with fewer than 200 cases described worldwide. Due to its rarity and nonspecific clinical presentation, it is frequently misdiagnosed as more common inguinoscrotal conditions such as hernia or hydrocele. Histologically, liposarcomas comprise several subtypes with varying prognoses. Accurate diagnosis is often challenging preoperatively and typically relies on imaging and definitive histopathological evaluation. CASE REPORT We present the case of an 87-year-old man with a progressively enlarging, painless mass in the left inguinoscrotal region, significantly impairing mobility. Computed tomography revealed a large, well-circumscribed mass originating from the spermatic cord, with both cystic and fatty components, along with a concurrent inguinal hernia and hydrocele. No metastatic spread was identified. The patient underwent complete surgical excision of the tumor with simultaneous orchiectomy and inguinal herniotomy. Histopathological analysis confirmed a well-differentiated liposarcoma (G1) with negative surgical margins (R0 resection). Given the patient's advanced age and comorbidities, no adjuvant therapy was indicated. The postoperative course was uneventful. CONCLUSIONS Spermatic cord liposarcoma remains a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge due to its rarity and clinical resemblance to benign conditions. Radical surgical excision with negative margins is the cornerstone of treatment and offers favorable outcomes, particularly in well-differentiated, low-grade tumors. However, the high rate of local recurrence necessitates long-term follow-up. The role of adjuvant therapies such as radiotherapy or chemotherapy remains unclear and should be individualized based on tumor characteristics. Increased awareness and reporting of such cases are essential to improve diagnostic accuracy and optimize management strategies.

title: Long-duration volumetric optoretinography enables measurement of retinal recovery dynamics after photostimulation.
abstract: Optoretinography (ORG) typically measures rapid photoreceptor responses, limiting investigation of slower retinal recovery processes. Here, we demonstrate long-duration volumetric ORG using customized high-resolution spectral-domain optical coherence tomography with repeated volumetric acquisition. Spatial averaging across the retinal volume improves sensitivity to both light-evoked scattering and outer segment (OS) optical path length (OPL) changes, while automated deep learning-based segmentation enables efficient analysis of large four-dimensional (4D) datasets. In vivo experiments in mice reveal distinct phases of retinal recovery dynamics extending over 30 min after photostimulation. Preliminary comparative measurements further reveal altered recovery behavior and an attenuated early OS OPL response in aged mice. This work establishes long-duration volumetric ORG as a platform for functional imaging of retinal physiological recovery dynamics in vivo.

title: Comparative evaluation of convolutional and transformer-based object detection models for brain tumor localization in MRI.
abstract: There is a need to detect and precisely localize brain tumors based on medical imaging to ensure such tumors are diagnosed early and treated with the aim of a successful treatment. More recent developments in the field of deep learning have presented convolution-based and transformer-based object detection models that can be used to achieve high detection rates. We carry out an analogous comparison of YOLOv11s and RF-DETR(small) in brain tumor detection on annotated Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) data on Roboflow in this study. Precision, Recall and mean Average Precision (mAP) along with localization loss measures were used to train and test both models. Findings indicate that YOLOv11s performed better in terms of mAP@50 of 95.2 percent, precision of 93.6 percent, and recall of 91 percent compared to RF-DETR that reported mAP@50 of 94.3 percent, precision of 90.6 percent, and recall of 85 percent. The findings point to the improved performance of YOLOv11s to localize and classify tumor locations in varying MRI slices. YOLOv11s with less convergent dynamic training behavior and RF-DETR(small) with better localization based on more challenging Intersection over Union (IoU) thresholds. The primary challenge was ensuring a fair comparison between two fundamentally different detection paradigms that employ distinct feature-learning mechanisms, pretraining schemes, optimization settings, and computational characteristics. Despite these, our findings highlight the feasibility of integrating advanced object detection models into computer-aided diagnostic tools for robust brain tumor detection in complex MRI data.

title: Adult Colocolonic Intussusception Temporally Associated With Curcumin Qingdai Use in a Patient With Ulcerative Proctitis.
abstract: Adult intussusception is rare and typically associated with an identifiable structural lead point. Emerging evidence suggests that herbal medications, including indigo naturalis, a component of curcumin QingDai, may be linked to gastrointestinal complications. We report a case of ascending colonic intussusception in a 42-year-old woman with ulcerative proctitis 5 weeks after initiating curcumin QingDai. Imaging confirmed the diagnosis, and surgical resection was required after failed conservative and endoscopic management. Histopathology revealed no structural lead point but showed inflammatory changes consistent with previous reports of indigo naturalis-associated injury. The temporal relationship and absence of alternative etiology support a possible association.

title: Successful Nonsurgical Management of Norovirus-Triggered Necrotizing Enterocolitis in a Preterm Infant: What Is the Role of Immunomodulation?
abstract: Norovirus infection has been increasingly recognized as a potential trigger of necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) in preterm neonates. Although previous reports have described severe cases associated with intestinal pneumatosis, bowel ischemia, and the need for surgical intervention, the clinical spectrum of Norovirus-related intestinal disease remains poorly defined. We report the case of a 29-week gestational age preterm infant who developed abdominal distension on the 35th day of life. Stool reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction confirmed Norovirus infection. Abdominal radiographs showed progressive development of intestinal pneumatosis, leading to the confirmed diagnosis of a stage IIA NEC. Abdominal pneumatosis resolved completely within five days, without evidence of perforation or clinical deterioration. The infant received only supportive therapy and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG). This case highlighted the heterogeneous clinical spectrum of Norovirus-associated intestinal involvement in preterm infants and the possible protective and immunomodulatory role of the IVIG.

title: Liposomal bupivacaine versus ropivacaine thoracic paravertebral block for thoracoscopic atrial septal defect repair: analgesic efficacy and cardiac biomarker outcomes in a single-center, assessor-blinded, randomized trial.
abstract: Background Thoracoscopic atrial septal defect (ASD) repair, although minimally invasive, can cause substantial postoperative pain. Thoracic paravertebral block (TPVB) provides effective chest wall analgesia, and liposomal bupivacaine (LB), a long-acting local anesthetic with sustained release, may prolong analgesic duration. We investigated whether ultrasound-guided TPVB using long-acting LB improves postoperative analgesia without compromising cardiovascular safety compared with ropivacaine (RP). Methods This randomized, assessor-blinded trial enrolled 94 patients undergoing thoracoscopic ASD repair, who were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive ultrasound-guided TPVB with either LB or RP. Eligibility criteria included age 18-55 years, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) II-III, New York Heart Association (NYHA) II-III, and ejection fraction (EF) >50%. Randomization was computer-generated with sealed envelopes. Safety monitoring included continuous electrocardiography (ECG) for arrhythmias, with Clavien-Dindo grading and Naranjo causality assessment. The primary endpoint was the numerical rating scale (NRS, 0-10) pain score during coughing at 24 h postoperatively. Secondary outcomes included NRS scores at other time points, 72-h opioid consumption (morphine milligram equivalents, MME), time to first rescue analgesia, extended analgesia outcomes [postoperative days 4-7 (POD4-POD7)], perioperative hemodynamics, postoperative recovery, cardiac/inflammatory biomarker trajectories, and adverse events (with postoperative arrhythmias analyzed separately). Results Baseline demographic, clinical, and intraoperative variables were well-balanced between groups (all P>0.05). Compared with RP, LB was associated with lower NRS pain scores at rest and during coughing from extubation through 72 h (all P<0.05), including the primary endpoint at 24 h. LB significantly reduced 72-h opioid consumption [median interquartile range (IQR) 7.5 (0, 42) mg vs. 45 (30, 67.5) mg; P<0.001] and increased the proportion of patients requiring no rescue analgesia within 72 h (72.4% vs. 27.6%; P=0.003). Time to first rescue analgesia was numerically longer with LB (20.5 h vs. 12.0 h; P=0.10), and opioid-sparing effects persisted on POD4-POD7 (both P<0.001). Mechanical ventilation duration was shorter in the LB group [5 (3, 6) h vs. 6 (4, 7.5) h; P=0.03]. Cardiac and inflammatory biomarker trajectories did not differ between groups. Non-arrhythmic adverse events were comparable, and postoperative arrhythmia incidence within 30 days was similar between groups (13.3% vs. 15.6%). Conclusions In adults undergoing thoracoscopic ASD repair, LB-based TPVB provides superior early analgesia with sustained opioid sparing and shorter mechanical ventilation duration, without signals of increased cardiovascular risk, including postoperative arrhythmias. These findings support considering LB-TPVB as part of multimodal analgesia for thoracoscopic ASD repair, pending confirmation in larger multicenter studies. Trial registration ChiCTR2500112278, retrospectively registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry on November 12, 2025.

LB significantly reduced 72-h opioid consumption [median interquartile range (IQR) 7.5 (0, 42) mg vs. 45 (30, 67.5) mg; P<0.001] and increased the proportion of patients requiring no rescue analgesia within 72 h (72.4% vs. 27.6%; P=0.003). Time to first rescue analgesia was numerically longer with LB (20.5 h vs. 12.0 h; P=0.10), and opioid-sparing effects persisted on POD4-POD7 (both P<0.001). Mechanical ventilation duration was shorter in the LB group [5 (3, 6) h vs. 6 (4, 7.5) h; P=0.03]. Cardiac and inflammatory biomarker trajectories did not differ between groups. Non-arrhythmic adverse events were comparable, and postoperative arrhythmia incidence within 30 days was similar between groups (13.3% vs. 15.6%).

Conclusions

In adults undergoing thoracoscopic ASD repair, LB-based TPVB provides superior early analgesia with sustained opioid sparing and shorter mechanical ventilation duration, without signals of increased cardiovascular risk, including postoperative arrhythmias. These findings support considering LB-TPVB as part of multimodal analgesia for thoracoscopic ASD repair, pending confirmation in larger multicenter studies.

title: Pyogenic Liver Abscess Following ERCP and Biliary Stenting: A Case Series of Two Patients and Clinical Implications
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) is a critical diagnostic and therapeutic modality for choledocholithiasis, acute cholangitis, and obstructive jaundice. Although pyogenic liver abscess is a rare complication following ERCP, it carries significant clinical implications. We present two cases of pyogenic liver abscess developing after ERCP and biliary stent-related procedures in patients with choledocholithiasis. Case Presentation: Case 1 involved a 42-year-old female who developed a liver abscess in segment 4 following laparoscopic cholecystectomy, common bile duct exploration, intraoperative ERCP with stent placement, primary closure of the common bile duct, and drainage of a segment 4 hepatic cyst. The abscess manifested after stent removal and balloon sweeping of the bile duct, presenting with right upper quadrant pain, chills, and fever up to 39°C. Computed tomography (CT) confirmed a liver abscess in segment 4. Case 2 involved a 62-year-old male who underwent ERCP with sphincterotomy, basket stone extraction, and biliary stent placement for choledocholithiasis with obstructive jaundice. On postoperative day 6, he developed right upper quadrant pain, chills, and fever up to 39°C. CT revealed a new 32 mm × 26 mm abscess in the right hepatic lobe, with markedly elevated procalcitonin (63.7 ng/mL) and renal dysfunction. Both patients improved after percutaneous drainage, and Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae were isolated from abscess cultures in both cases. Conclusion: Although rare, pyogenic liver abscess should be considered in patients with biliary infection, stent placement or removal, sphincterotomy, complex biliary surgery, or pre-existing hepatic cystic lesions following ERCP. Early imaging evaluation with ultrasonography or contrast-enhanced CT is warranted when postoperative abdominal pain, chills, high fever, elevated inflammatory markers, or cholestasis abnormalities occur. Image-guided percutaneous drainage, combined with appropriate antimicrobial therapy, serves as an effective minimally invasive intervention for source control.

title: Cryptogenic Near-Complete Left Internal Carotid Artery Occlusion in a 20-Year-Old Male: A Diagnostic and Pharmacological Challenge.
abstract: Abstract Background Large vessel occlusions (LVO), particularly those involving the internal carotid artery (ICA), are exceedingly rare in young adults. These events typically prompt aggressive screening for underlying prothrombotic and metabolic disorders. Case presentation A 20-year-old male presented with severe headache, slurred speech, right-sided seizures, and hemiplegia. Magnetic Resonance Angiography (MRA) identified a near-complete occlusion of the intracranial segments of the left ICA. Despite the severe cerebrovascular event, comprehensive screening for metabolic and hypercoagulability factors remained unremarkable, which notably included a strictly normal baseline serum homocysteine level of 6.67 µmol/L. The patient was successfully managed with aggressive dual antithrombotic therapy alongside empirical folic acid supplementation. During regular clinical follow-ups every 2 months over a 2-year period, the patient demonstrated significant neurological recovery without any recurrent ischemic events. Conclusion This case underscores the diagnostic challenges associated with cryptogenic LVOs in young adults. It emphasizes the likelihood of spontaneous arterial dissection when metabolic anomalies are absent. Furthermore, the case discusses the pharmacological rationale for utilizing empirical metabolic interventions in cases of unexplained early-onset stroke.

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted prediction of Xpert-confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis using routine clinical and laboratory data in Southern Zambia: a retrospective pilot study
abstract: Abstract Background Artificial intelligence has shown promise for tuberculosis screening, particularly through automated chest radiograph interpretation. Its usefulness when applied to routinely collected clinical and laboratory data in district-level African settings is less certain. We assessed whether simple machine-learning models could predict Xpert-confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis using routine surveillance data from a clinical laboratory in Southern Zambia. Methods We performed a retrospective pilot prediction study using tuberculosis surveillance records from Namwala District Hospital and referring facilities. Records without a valid GeneXpert result were excluded, and duplicate study numbers were reduced to one diagnostic episode. The outcome was Mycobacterium tuberculosis detected versus not detected by Xpert MTB/RIF. Descriptive comparisons, univariable logistic regression and a parsimonious multivariable model were undertaken. Logistic regression, random forest and gradient boosting models using body mass index and specimen type were evaluated with repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation (20 repeats). Model performance was described by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), precision-recall AUC and Brier score. Bootstrap internal validation was used for the final logistic model. Results Of 129 records, 8 lacked a GeneXpert outcome and 3 duplicate records were removed, leaving 118 unique diagnostic episodes. MTB was detected in 17 patients (14.4%, 95% CI 9.2–21.9). Median age was 30 years, 63 (53.4%) participants were male, 42 (35.6%) were HIV positive and 95 (80.5%) were inpatients. Saliva-labelled specimens were positive in 4 of 7 cases (57.1%), compared with 13 of 109 non-saliva specimens (11.9%). Saliva remained associated with MTB detection after adjustment for body mass index (adjusted OR 10.55, 95% CI 2.09–53.37; P = 0.004), although the estimate was imprecise. Cross-validated AUROC was 0.593 for logistic regression, 0.522 for random forest and 0.596 for gradient boosting. The final logistic model had an optimism-corrected AUROC of 0.666 and Brier score of 0.121. Conclusions Routine clinical and laboratory variables had limited ability to predict Xpert-confirmed tuberculosis in this small real-world dataset. The association with saliva-labelled specimens is hypothesis-generating and requires verification. The models are not suitable for clinical deployment or exclusion of patients from molecular testing. Larger, prospectively curated, multicentre Zambian datasets are required before artificial intelligence can support tuberculosis diagnostic prioritisation in routine care.

title: ThyroGuard-Net: A Sensitivity-Optimised, Explainable Hybrid CNN–Transformer Framework with Evidential Uncertainty for Thyroid Nodule Classification
abstract: Abstract Thyroid cancer is a common endocrine malignancy and the most common diagnostic technique for thyroid cancer is ultrasound-guided fine needle aspiration (FNA) cytology. Although many researchers have utilized machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), recent studies still rely on small single-centre datasets, poor generalisation across institutions, class imbalance, lack of explainability and – crucially – insufficient focus on sensitivity. This article highlights the typical issues that have plagued studies over the past decade and offers the recommendation of a publicly available, relatively multi-center dataset, TN3K that can help mitigate those issues. This paper proposes a hybrid EfficientNet–Swin Transformer architecture for robust and efficient training of concept-attention networks, trained with a sensitivity-weighted Focal-Tversky loss, an evidential uncertainty module for indeterminate-case triage and a concept-bottleneck explainability layer based on TI-RADS. It presents a complete mathematical formulation for all components (pre-processing, dual-branch feature extraction, cross-attention fusion, concept-bottleneck explainability, sensitivity-maximising loss design, and evidential uncertainty estimation). The model was trained on TN3K and tested without further fine tuning on the external DDTI dataset with 87.95%/91.46%/85.60% (accuracy/sensitivity/specificity) on the test set, with an evidential triage rate of 13.03–16.95%, showing the cross-institution generalisation narrowed and clinically, calibrated uncertainty over previous single-mechanism methods.

title: Cone-Beam CT–Guided Thin Linear EBUS Bronchoscopic Biopsy of a Non- Peripheral Lung Nodule: Highlighting the Effect of Bronchoscopic Tools on CT-to-Body Divergence: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Accurate bronchoscopic biopsy of non-peripheral pulmonary nodules adjacent to proximal segmental airways remains challenging. Such lesions lie beyond the reach of standard endobronchial ultrasound transbronchial needle aspiration (EBUS-TBNA) and resist accurate bronchoscope angulation in proximal, less flexible bronchi. Case presentation: A 43-year-old non-smoking male was referred for biopsy of an incidentally found 16-mm solid right upper lobe nodule located adjacent to the second subsegmental branch (RB3b). The procedure was performed under general anaesthesia using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT)–guided thin linear EBUS bronchoscopy (UCP190F, Olympus; 5.9-mm distal diameter). Intraprocedural CBCT acquisition enabled nodule segmentation and biopsy pathway planning overlaid on augmented fluoroscopy. Real-time ultrasound confirmed lesion localisation. During close-range bronchoscope manipulation, articulation of the bronchoscope tip caused reproducible displacement of the lesion relative to the augmented fluoroscopic target — a phenomenon we term bronchoscope- or tool-induced divergence, distinct from the established concept of CT-to-body divergence. Fine-needle aspiration under simultaneous ultrasound and augmented fluoroscopic guidance, with rapid on-site cytology, confirmed lesional material. Three cryobiopsies were then obtained using a 1.1-mm cryoprobe (Erbe, Tübingen) via the working channel in a wedged, stabilised position. The patient was discharged the same day; histopathology confirmed a typical carcinoid tumour. Conclusions: CBCT-guided bronchoscopy using a thin linear EBUS bronchoscope is feasible for non-peripheral lung nodules in anatomically challenging locations. Awareness of bronchoscope- and tool-induced divergence is clinically relevant and should be considered alongside CT-to-body divergence when targeting accuracy is suboptimal, particularly in proximal airways.

title: Low-grade Oncocytic Fumarate Hydratase-deficient Renal Cell Carcinoma in a Patient with Hereditary Leiomyomatosis and Renal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Fumarate hydratase (FH)-deficient renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is generally an aggressive, high-grade tumor with a poor prognosis. We report a case of low-grade oncocytic FH-deficient RCC with a favorable course and discuss it in the context of the genotype-phenotype relationship in FH-deficient RCC. Case presentation: A woman in her 70s was found to have bilateral multifocal renal tumors on PET-CT performed during the work-up of a left cervical mass. She underwent robot-assisted partial nephrectomy of the left kidney. Histopathology showed a low-grade oncocytic renal tumor (pT1aNXMX, WHO/ISUP grade 2) without sarcomatoid change or necrosis, and immunohistochemistry demonstrated loss of FH expression with 2SC positivity, establishing the diagnosis of low-grade oncocytic FH-deficient RCC. Germline genetic testing identified a heterozygous FH missense variant, c.584T > C (p.Met195Thr), confirming hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma (HLRCC) syndrome. The pedigree showed maternal-line uterine leiomyomatosis consistent with autosomal dominant transmission. The postoperative course was uneventful, with no recurrence or metastasis. The cervical mass proved to be a benign thyroid nodule unrelated to the renal tumor. Conclusion FH-deficient RCC can present as a low-grade, organ-confined tumor with a favorable course. The identical germline FH variant (p.Met195Thr) has elsewhere caused an aggressive tumor, underscoring that the germline genotype does not by itself determine prognosis. Management according to FH-deficient RCC and genetic counseling of relatives remain essential.

title: A Gigantic Heterogenous Silent Corticotroph Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumour With Posterior Fossa Cyst and a Fibrotic Wall—Diagnostic Mimicry and Route-Tailored Staging: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Neurosurgical route selection for treating silent corticotroph pituitary neuroendocrine tumours is complicated because of their nature of mimicking aggressive skull-base disease. Case presentation: A 21-year-old man with a background of autism spectrum disorder presented with headache, diplopia, right third cranial nerve palsy and visual blurring. A giant heterogeneous sellar–suprasellar mass with cavernous sinus/internal carotid artery involvement and a posterior fossa cyst compressing the brainstem is shown on MRI. He has a normal baseline pituitary test result. Endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal debulking achieved diagnosis and decompression; histology confirmed a silent corticotroph pituitary neuroendocrine tumour (adrenocorticotropic hormone-positive, limited T-box pituitary transcription factor. Post-operative diabetes insipidus occurred. On surveillance, the cyst enlarged with hydrocephalus. Two Ommaya attempts failed due to a taut, fibrotic wall. Right craniotomy enabled lateral debulking and direct cyst cannulation with effective decompression. Residual cavernous/internal carotid artery-adjacent disease was treated with proton beam therapy (50.4 Gy/28 fractions) without notable acute toxicity. Bulbar function and third-nerve palsy improved post-craniotomy; gait and speech improved after radiotherapy. Imaging showed reduced brainstem compression with a manageable residual; visual acuity remained 6/21 right, 6/6 left. Conclusions: This case supports route-tailored staging-endonasal decompression, early conversion to transcranial access for fibrotic, catheter-resistant cysts, and consolidative proton therapy-and highlights the value of autism spectrum disorder-adapted pathways and multidisciplinary team oversight.

title: Feature Fusion Based Deep Learning Framework for Brain Tumor Classification
abstract: Abstract Classification is considered very important step in diagnosis of serious diseases like brain tumor as it plays an important role in prognosis and successful recovery of the patient. This paper proposes an explainable hybrid deep learning architecture for seven class brain tumor classification using feature-level fusion of six independently fine-tuned pre-trained CNN models: Xception, InceptionV3, VGG16, MobileNetV2, ResNet50, and DenseNet121. Fifteen feature level fusion combinations have been evaluated using a dataset of 11,288 MRI scans representing six tumor classes and one nontumor class: glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, astrocytoma, ependymoma, schwannoma. InceptionV3 + VGG16, the hybrid architecture gave best performance according to experimental results attaining test accuracy of 97.87% with outstanding macro and weighted F1-scores of 97.77% and 97.87% subsequently. Further, Grad-CAM and Occlusion Sensitivity Analysis were collectively implemented on classification results of best hybrid model to ensure the clinical relevance of the learned features and offering visual explanations of the classification. Finally, best hybrid model was successfully validated on external dataset of five tumor classes comprising 234 MRI scans to prove its generalization on unseen dataset.

title: Parents’ experiences of whole-body MRI-based surveillance for their child with genetic cancer risk: a longitudinal qualitative study
abstract: Abstract Broad genomic screening in pediatric oncology is increasingly identifying children with genetic cancer risk indicating intensive, lifelong surveillance. While this may improve early cancer detection, families face complex psychosocial challenges with unclear implications for adherence. We aimed to explore parents’ experiences of ongoing surveillance for their child with a multi-organ genetic cancer risk condition, including how these experiences changed over time. Parents’/caregivers’ of children (<18yrs) participating in WBMRI-based surveillance completed interviews at enrolment and following surveillance events. Interviews were transcribed and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Thirteen parents (median age=41.4yrs; 54% female) of 13 children (median age=8.1yrs) participated in 33 interviews (median=2, range=1-5). Children had germline pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in TP53 (n=10), BLM (n=2; biallelic), and RB1 (n=1) genes. Parents described surveillance as characterized by cyclical procedural and outcome-related uncertainty influenced by additional psychosocial stressors. Coping strategies evolved over time and involved emotional (e.g. compartmentalization) and practical strategies (e.g. simulating procedures). Administrative burdens, care co-ordination, and persistent fear of cancer occurrence remained significant challenges. Parents’ initially described children as focused on procedural aspects of surveillance, for some these perceptions shifted across repeated surveillance with some children showing increased cancer-related distress. A desire to benefit their child, seek reassurance, and contribute to research motivated ongoing engagement despite challenges. Parents perceive surveillance as worthwhile, despite emotional and practical burdens. Multidisciplinary care models that streamline communication and integrate proactive psychosocial and dedicated psychological support may reduce ongoing challenges.

Administrative burdens, care co-ordination, and persistent fear of cancer occurrence remained significant challenges. Parents’ initially described children as focused on procedural aspects of surveillance, for some these perceptions shifted across repeated surveillance with some children showing increased cancer-related distress. A desire to benefit their child, seek reassurance, and contribute to research motivated ongoing engagement despite challenges. Parents perceive surveillance as worthwhile, despite emotional and practical burdens. Multidisciplinary care models that streamline communication and integrate proactive psychosocial and dedicated psychological support may reduce ongoing challenges.

title: Extranodal Rosai Dorfman Disease: An Unusual Course Without Nodal or Systemic Involvement- Case report
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Rosai–Dorfman disease (RDD) is a rare benign non-Langerhans cell histiocytic disorder that typically presents with painless cervical lymphadenopathy. Isolated extranodal disease involving the head and neck is uncommon, while recurrent multifocal disease without nodal or systemic involvement is exceptionally rare. We report a unique case of recurrent multifocal extranodal RDD confined to the sinonasal tract and eyelid. Case Report: A woman in her late 50s presented with recurrent nasal obstruction and epistaxis. Evaluation revealed a mass in the right nasal cavity, which was excised endoscopically. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of extranodal RDD. During a 3-year follow-up, she experienced sequential recurrences involving the contralateral nasal cavity, nasal septum, anterior ethmoid sinus, and left lower eyelid. Each lesion was managed successfully with complete surgical excision, and histopathology consistently confirmed recurrent RDD. Despite multifocal recurrences, there was no evidence of cervical lymphadenopathy, systemic symptoms, or radiological features of aggressive disease. The patient remained symptom-free following each surgery and did not require systemic therapy. Conclusion This case highlights an unusual presentation of recurrent multifocal extranodal RDD involving the sinonasal tract and eyelid in the absence of nodal or systemic disease. Although recurrence is uncommon, RDD should be considered in the differential diagnosis of recurrent sinonasal masses. Histopathological confirmation remains essential for diagnosis, and complete surgical excision can provide excellent long-term disease control in patients with localized recurrent extranodal disease, avoiding the need for systemic treatment.

title: Multimodal Study of Brain Structural Alterations, Functional Gradient Perturbations, and Transcriptomic Specialization in Trigeminal Neuralgia Using 5.0 Tesla MRI
abstract: Abstract Objective: This study aimed to harness the superior imaging capability of 5.0 T MRI to comprehensively characterize structural brain alterations, functional connectome gradient perturbations, and their underlying transcriptomic correlates in patients with trigeminal neuralgia (TN). By constructing an interpretative framework linking macroscopic gradient changes to microscale gene specialization. Methods: Thirty‑five TN patients and sixty‑four healthy controls (HC) were enrolled. All participants underwent 3D high‑resolution T1 and resting‑state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) on a 5.0 T scanner. Functional connectome gradients were derived from the functional connectivity (FC) matrix via diffusion map embedding. Gray matter volume (GMV) was computed using voxel‑based morphometry (VBM), and structure‑function coupling was assessed via spatial correlations. Partial least squares (PLS) regression was employed to identify gene sets associated with gradient perturbations, followed by enrichment analysis to reveal the underlying biological processes. Results: TN patients exhibited attenuated extreme values and increased intermediate values on the primary gradient, with altered gradient scores across multiple networks, indicative of a global gradient compression. GMV reductions was observed in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and superior frontal gyrus (SFG), while gradient scores were decreased in the mPFC and ventral anterior cingulate cortex (vACC). Spatial correlation analyses revealed structure‑function decoupling in the sensorimotor (SMN), limbic (LIB), and frontoparietal (FPN) networks. Transcriptomic analyses showed that cortical gradient perturbations were strongly associated with genes involved in voltage‑gated ion channels, membrane potential regulation, and neurotransmitter release. Significant enrichment of sodium channel, Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase, and GABA receptor genes further corroborated the ion channelopathy basis of TN. Conclusion: 5.0T MRI-based connectome gradient analysis reveals global compression and network-specific reorganization in TN. mPFC/vACC dedifferentiation reflects hierarchical collapse of descending pain inhibition, underpinning chronification. Gene enrichment corroborates ion channelopathy and suggests novel targets. This multi-scale framework integrates structure, function, and transcriptomics to advance mechanistic insights.

title: Prognostic value of pretreatment sarcopenia in unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma treated with yttrium-90 radioembolization
abstract: Abstract Objective Sarcopenia is a prognostic biomarker in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but its impact after transarterial radioembolization (TARE) with yttrium-90 ( 90 Y) microspheres and its relationship with tumor absorbed dose remain unclear. We assessed the prognostic value of sarcopenia for local progression-free survival (LPFS), progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS) in patients with HCC treated with TARE. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 75 patients with HCC treated with 90Y glass or resin microspheres between June 2022 and December 2024. Skeletal muscle index (SMI) was derived from the CT component of [ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ([ 18 F]FDG PET/CT) at L3. Sarcopenia was defined using sex- and BMI-specific SMI cut-offs. Tumor absorbed dose was dichotomized at 485 Gy. Survival was assessed by Kaplan–Meier analysis, and prognostic factors were evaluated using Cox regression. Results Sarcopenia was present in 32 patients (42.7%). Compared with non-sarcopenic patients, sarcopenic patients had lower objective response (34.4% vs. 97.7%; p < 0.001) and disease control rates (62.5% vs. 100%; p < 0.001). Median LPFS, PFS, and OS were 6, 6, and 10 months in sarcopenic patients versus 21, 19 months, and not reached in non-sarcopenic patients (all p < 0.001). On multivariable analysis, sarcopenia independently predicted shorter LPFS (HR 4.0; 95% CI 2.1–7.7; p < 0.001), PFS (HR 2.8; 95% CI 1.6–5.2; p < 0.001), and OS (HR 5.5; 95% CI 2.5–12.0; p < 0.001). Tumor absorbed dose < 485 Gy independently predicted shorter LPFS (HR 1.9; 95% CI 1.1–3.6; p = 0.034), but not PFS (HR 1.7; 95% CI 0.94–3.0; p = 0.078) or OS (HR 1.7; 95% CI 0.81–3.6; p = 0.161). Conclusion Pretreatment sarcopenia is an independent predictor of LPFS, PFS, and OS after TARE for HCC. Tumor absorbed dose remains associated with local tumor control, but an adequate dose does not overcome the adverse prognosis associated with sarcopenia. Routine assessment of skeletal muscle mass may improve risk stratification and help identify patients requiring closer surveillance and earlier systemic therapy.

title: Prognostic Value of PSMA Dominance on Dual-Tracer PET in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Prospective Single-Center Study
abstract: Abstract Background To evaluate the prognostic value of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) findings in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and to assess its incremental prognostic value over fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography (PET) and established clinical factors. Methods In this prospective, single-center study, 18 patients with HCC (mean age: 65.3±11.5years, 78%male) underwent dual-tracer PSMA and FDG PET imaging for staging (n=14) and restaging (n=4), with a median interval of 6 days between scans. Clinical variables, including age, gender, serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) grade, and Child-Pugh class, as well as imaging parameters derived from PSMA and FDG PET, were evaluated. Time to progression (TTP) and overall survival (OS) were assessed using the Kaplan–Meier method and compared with the log-rank test. Cox proportional hazards regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictors of survival. PSMA dominance was defined as PSMA-dominant uptake (PSMA>FDG). Results During a median follow-up of 15.5 months, 11 patients (61.1%) developed disease progression and 9 (50.0%) died. In Kaplan–Meier analysis, several clinical and imaging variables were associated with OS, including ascites, ALBI grade, Child-Pugh class, PSMA PET positivity, PSMA-detected extrahepatic disease (EHD), FDG-detected portal vein thrombosis (PVT), and PSMA dominance. For TTP, ascites, ALBI grade, Child-Pugh class, PSMA-detected EHD, and PVT detected on both PSMA and FDG were significant. In multivariable Cox analysis, PSMA dominance emerged as an independent predictor of OS (HR: 37.85, 95% CI:2.42-592.84, p = 0.010), together with Child-Pugh class (HR: 81.02, 95% CI:4.09-1603.51, p = 0.004) and AFP ≥200 ng/mL (HR: 13.86, 95% CI:1.41-135.91, p = 0.024). For TTP, ascites (HR: 48.82, 95% CI:X-Y, p = 0.004) and PSMA-detected EHD (HR: 16.28, 95% CI:X-Y, p = 0.024) remained independently associated with shorter TTP. Conclusion In HCC, disease progression appears to be primarily driven by tumor burden and extent, whereas overall survival is additionally influenced by liver function and tumor biology. Among PET-derived markers, PSMA dominance emerged as a potential imaging biomarker and was independently associated with overall survival, suggesting that the incremental prognostic value of PSMA PET may lie primarily in its ability to capture biologic heterogeneity beyond FDG PET alone.

title: Relative contributions of reconstruction pipeline and MRI field strength to hippocampal shape variation
abstract: Abstract Objective Ultra-high-field 7T MRI provides increased signal-to-noise ratio and spatial resolution compared with 3T MRI, but contributions of field strength and reconstruction methodology to whole-hippocampus shape remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated their relative contributions to hippocampal shape variation. Materials and Methods MRI data were acquired from ten healthy adults scanned at 3T and 7T in a within-subject design. Right hippocampal 3D models were reconstructed using FSL, FreeSurfer, HippUnfold, and manual segmentation. Shape was quantified using geometric morphometrics based on 97 landmarks and semilandmarks. Procrustes ANOVA assessed effects of subject, reconstruction pipeline, and field strength. Results Subject was the principal source of hippocampal shape variation ( R² =0.194, P < 0.0001), followed by reconstruction pipeline ( R² =0.050, P = 0.0003) and field strength ( R² =0.025, P < 0.0001). Field strength and reconstruction pipeline interacted significantly ( R² =0.045, P = 0.0022). Hippocampal size showed significant agreement between field strengths ( r = 0.741, P < 0.0001), whereas shape correspondence was weaker but significant ( r = 0.371, P < 0.0001). FSL showed the smallest within-subject 3T–7T shape differences and closest agreement with manual segmentation. Discussion In this pilot cohort, reconstruction methodology had greater influence than field strength. Field-strength-related differences were modest relative to inter-individual and methodological effects, supporting whole-hippocampus morphometric analyses using 3T MRI under the evaluated imaging conditions.

title: Pitfalls of enzyme- based diagnosis of lysosomal storage diseases in children
abstract: Abstract Background: Fabry disease is uniquely inherited in an X-linked manner, in contrast to the autosomal recessive inheritance observed in Pompe, Gaucher, Niemann–Pick diseases, and Mucopolysaccharidoses (except Hunter disease). Each disorder is characterized by deficiency of a specific lysosomal enzyme, leading to accumulation of distinct substrates and subsequent organ-specific pathology. Purpose: This study aimed to assess the concordance between clinical findings, enzymatic, substrate and genetic testing in patients suspected of having rare lysosomal storage disorders (LSDs), with emphasis on cases showing diagnostic discordance, where enzyme assay and clinical evidence supports a disease despite negative ꜠substrate accumulation and genetic ꜠ results. Patients and Methods: The study included 46 cases from El-beheira governorate. Enzyme assay, substrate and genetic analysis were performed using the ARCHIMED life International Medical Laboratory platform, which offers testing for rare diseases with unlimited reanalysis incorporating newly discovered conditions until a diagnosis is achieved. Next generation Sequencing (NGS) was used for gene sequencing, while enzyme levels and their corresponding substrates were measured using tandem mass spectrometry from dried blood spots. Clinical evaluation of affected organs was conducted at the Damanhur Teaching Hospital by using Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). Results: Analysis of the selected LSDs demonstrated marked genetic and enzymatic heterogeneity despite shared lysosomal dysfunction. Hunter disease (MPS type 2) is uniquely inherited in an X-linked recessive manner. In contrast, Pompe disease, Gaucher disease, Niemann–Pick disease, and the rest of types of Mucopolysaccharidoses followed an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern. Each disorder was associated with deficiency of a specific lysosomal enzyme, leading to accumulation of distinct substrates, including glycogen in Pompe disease, glucocerebroside (glucosylsphingosine) in Gaucher disease, sphingomyelins in NPD and glycosaminoglycans (GAGs) in MPS. Conclusion: This study identified patients with reduced enzyme activity and supportive clinical features despite negative genetic findings and normal substrate levels. These results highlight the limitations of relying solely on enzyme testing and emphasize the importance of integrated clinical, enzymatic, substrate accumulation and molecular assessment for accurate diagnosis and management.

title: Nodular lymphocyte predominant B-cell lymphoma involving an intraparotid lymph node: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Nodular lymphocyte predominant B-cell lymphoma (formerly known as nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma) is a distinct B-cell neoplasm characterized by large neoplastic cells with multilobulated “popcorn-like” nuclei. It typically presents as peripheral lymphadenopathy and rarely involves the intraparotid lymph nodes, which may pose a diagnostic challenge due to overlap with other lymphoid neoplasms, particularly classical Hodgkin lymphoma. Case presentation: A 23-year-old man presented with a painless left parotid swelling. Ultrasound revealed a solitary intraparotid lymph node, and an excisional biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL). After the PET/CT scan, it was classified as Stage IA. He was treated with localized radiotherapy and remained clinically stable at 3-months follow up. Conclusion Nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL) rarely involves the parotid lymph nodes, presenting diagnostic challenges due to its indolent course and potential histologic mimicry of benign lesions. Accurate diagnosis requires excisional biopsy and immunohistochemistry, and treatment is stage-dependent. Despite a favorable prognosis, careful follow-up is essential because of the risk of relapse or transformation into aggressive B-cell lymphoma.

title: Associations Between Thalamic Gray Matter Volume and Psychomotor Symptoms in Major Depressive Disorder: A Voxel-Based Morphometry Study.
abstract: Background Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a heterogeneous disorder with diverse symptom profiles and treatment responses. Psychomotor retardation and agitation represent clinically relevant dimensions of MDD heterogeneity, but their neurobiological basis remains unclear. Given the role of the thalamus in motor regulation and affective processing, this study examined thalamic gray matter volume (GMV) differences among patients with MDD with predominant psychomotor retardation (MDD-R), patients with MDD with predominant psychomotor agitation (MDD-A), and healthy controls (HCs). Methods Structural MRI data from the REST-meta-MDD consortium included 54 patients with MDD-A, 123 with MDD-R, and 122 HCs. Total, hemispheric, and 30 subregional thalamic GMV measures were extracted using voxel-based morphometry and the AAL3v1 atlas. ComBat harmonization was applied before analysis. Group differences were tested with analysis of covariance controlling for sex, age, education, and total gray matter volume. Exploratory partial Spearman correlations examined associations with psychomotor symptoms, HAMD(adj), and anxiety symptoms. Results After FDR correction, significant group effects were limited to the bilateral ventral anterior nucleus (VA). Patients with MDD-R had greater bilateral VA GMV than HCs, whereas MDD-A did not differ from HCs. No direct MDD-A vs MDD-R difference survived FDR correction; only the left inferior pulvinar showed a nominal difference. Exploratory correlations linked several thalamic nuclei, including the reuniens nucleus, ventral posterolateral nucleus, lateral geniculate nucleus, and anteroventral nucleus, to psychomotor, depressive, or anxiety symptoms. Conclusion MDD-R was associated with selective bilateral VA structural differences rather than widespread thalamic abnormalities. No direct thalamic GMV difference between MDD-A and MDD-R survived FDR correction. The exploratory symptom associations suggest that thalamic structure may relate to multidimensional clinical heterogeneity in MDD. These findings require replication given the cross-sectional design, unequal subgroup sizes, and incomplete medication data.

title: The Future of AI in Breast Cancer: Quantum Computing and Next-Gen Algorithms for Precision Oncology.
abstract: Breast cancer is still one of the most significant global contributors to cancer-related deaths. Artificial intelligence (AI) applications in imaging, diagnostic imaging and assistance, systemic treatment and personalization, and predictive modeling are all part of the fast-growing field of breast cancer care. This review examined the many applications of AI in cancer care, including prediction, diagnostic work-up, staging, early diagnosis, and therapy response. AI's contributions to radiology include risk assessment models, tomosynthesis-enhanced mammography, and other imaging methods, including MRI and ultrasound. In pathology, AI can improve marker quantification and histological diagnosis, as well as prognostic models, including models for predicting genetic mutations. Realising the potential of AI, however, will not be without challenges that may limit ubiquity in clinical practice. Our review highlights the potentially transformational but presently limited ability of AI to improve breast cancer care. It urges targeted research to eliminate these obstacles and maximize the application of AIsupported solutions to those that impede clinical adoption in the real world. We have been able to demonstrate how AI may enhance diagnostic precision, customize treatment options, and have a favorable impact on patient outcomes from detection to treatment and follow-up care by methodically recording its involvement in radiology and pathology. The effectiveness of AI's influence on breast cancer treatment hinges on cooperation and regulatory compliance.

title: AI Decision Support for Emergency Triage of Large Vessel Occlusion Using Noncontrast Computed Tomography: Systematic Review and Bayesian Diagnostic Test Accuracy Network Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background Emergency triage of anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (LVO) is constrained by delays in vascular imaging, specialist interpretation, and transfer decision-making. Noncontrast computed tomography (NCCT) is often obtained first in suspected stroke, but visual recognition of LVO in NCCT images is difficult outside specialist settings. NCCT-based AI may provide an early human-in-the-loop escalation signal. Objective This study aimed to compare validated NCCT-based AI paradigms with human reader paradigms for detection of anterior circulation LVO and assess whether current evidence supports prospective evaluation of AI-assisted escalation pathways. Methods We searched the PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, and Cochrane Library databases from inception to May 24, 2026. Eligible studies evaluated NCCT-based LVO detection in validation datasets independent of model development, included within-study head-to-head comparisons, and provided reconstructible 2 × 2 data. Four nodes were compared: expert readers, nonexpert readers, unimodal imaging AI, and clinically informed multimodal AI. A Bayesian bivariate hierarchical diagnostic test accuracy network meta-analysis estimated sensitivity, specificity, diagnostic odds ratio, and absolute differences. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed using the Prediction Model Risk of Bias Assessment Tool for AI and the complementary Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-3, and certainty was rated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). Results All 10 included studies were retrospective validation studies, comprising 11 validation datasets, 28 study node arms, and 3632 patients. Unimodal imaging AI had a sensitivity of 0.78 (95% credible interval 0.68-0.86), specificity of 0.88 (95% credible interval 0.81-0.94), and diagnostic odds ratio of 30.89 (95% credible interval 14.19-60.27). Expert readers and nonexpert readers had lower sensitivity estimates of 0.62 (95% credible interval 0.48-0.75) and 0.60 (95% credible interval 0.45-0.75), respectively, with similar specificity estimates of 0.86. In league table comparisons, unimodal imaging AI showed higher sensitivity than expert and nonexpert readers by 0.16 (95% credible interval 0.03-0.29) and 0.18 (95% credible interval 0.03-0.32), respectively, with no clear specificity separation. Clinically informed multimodal AI had a sensitivity of 0.81 (95% credible interval 0.64-0.92) and specificity of 0.92 (95% credible interval 0.80-0.98), but this sparse node was connected to human readers only through indirect evidence. Conclusions In retrospective validation cohorts, there was low-certainty comparative evidence suggesting that NCCT-based AI, most clearly unimodal imaging AI, had higher sensitivity than human reader paradigms, without a clear difference in specificity. These findings support prospective evaluation of NCCT-based AI as a bounded human-in-the-loop prompt for expert review, computed tomography angiography prioritization, tele-stroke consultation, or transfer discussion. The evidence remains accuracy based and does not establish workflow effectiveness, reperfusion acceleration, or functional outcome benefit. Trial registration PROSPERO CRD420261362111; https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261362111.

title: Optimizing the Therapeutic Index: Sequential Intraarterial-Intravenous PRRT with Personalized Volumetric-Adjusted Dosing.
abstract: Patients with well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) frequently present with liver-dominant metastases, which significantly impact prognosis and limit curative options. Although standard intravenous peptide receptor radionuclide therapy with 177 Lu-DOTATATE is effective, strategies to intensify the radiation dose to hepatic lesions are needed to improve outcomes. This prospective clinical trial investigated the feasibility, tolerability, and preliminary efficacy of a personalized treatment schedule combining intraarterial and intravenous administrations of 177 Lu-DOTATATE. Methods: Ten consecutive adults with progressive, nonresectable, liver-dominant metastatic gastroenteropancreatic NETs expressing somatostatin receptors were enrolled. The treatment protocol comprised 4 cycles of 177 Lu-DOTATATE administered every 2 mo (2 initial intraarterial cycles followed by 2 intravenous cycles). Intraarterial administration involved angiographically guided, selective catheterization of the hepatic arteries with volumetrically adjusted activity to maximize targeted delivery. Safety monitoring, radiation protection, and dosimetry comparisons between intraarterial and intravenous routes were performed. Results: The intraarterial administration procedure was feasible in 100% of patients. Radiation exposure to staff and patients remained within regulatory limits, with no contamination events. Dosimetry analysis indicated that intraarterial administration (cycle 1) delivered a greater than 3-fold higher radiation dose to liver metastases compared with the intravenous route (cycle 3), although interim response may have played a role. Furthermore, 68 Ga-DOTATATE PET imaging revealed an 86% increase in median liver lesion uptake with intraarterial administration. The regimen was generally well-tolerated, with only 1 severe adverse event reported (low esophageal tear), which was not attributed to the administration route. Efficacy analysis showed partial response rates in 67% of patients at the first follow-up 3 mo after treatment completion, improving to 87% at the second follow-up (6 mo) in accordance with RECIST and volumetric criteria. Conclusion: The sequential administration of intraarterial followed by intravenous 177 Lu-DOTATATE is a feasible and safe therapeutic strategy for liver-dominant metastatic NETs. The use of a personalized, volumetric-based approach provided higher uptake and absorbed doses in hepatic metastases, with high objective response rates and effectively maintained systemic coverage.

title: Glypican-3 as a Theranostic Target in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
abstract: Glypican-3 (GPC3) has emerged as an attractive molecular target for the imaging and therapy of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). It is highly expressed in most tumors but shows no or minimal expression in the normal adult liver and cirrhosis. This expression profile has stimulated the parallel development of GPC3-directed antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, cellular immunotherapies, molecular imaging agents, and therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals. Early clinical imaging studies with radiolabeled antibodies established proof of principle that GPC3 can be visualized with PET imaging while also highlighting the pharmacokinetic limitations of full-size antibodies for liver imaging. More recent approaches using antibody fragments, single-domain antibodies, single-chain variable fragments, and macrocyclic peptides have substantially improved imaging contrast at earlier time points and have enabled first-in-human PET studies in patients with HCC and hepatoblastoma. These studies indicate the feasibility of GPC3-targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy but have also demonstrated intrapatient and interpatient heterogeneity of target expression, emphasizing the need for pretherapeutic imaging of GPC3 expression before therapeutic interventions. Thus, GPC3 imaging could contribute not only to the diagnosis and staging of HCC but also to treatment monitoring and the selection of patients for GPC3-targeted therapies. A clinical phase 1 trial with an 225 Ac-labeled macrocyclic peptide ([ 225 Ac]Ac-RAYZ-8009, RYZ801) using PET with [ 68 Ga]Ga-RAYZ-8009 (RYZ811) for patient selection is currently ongoing. Furthermore, an 225 Ac-labeled GPC3 antibody, BAY 3547926, is undergoing phase 1/2 clinical testing.
